name: Lebanese Atayef Asafiri (Ricotta-Stuffed Pancake) with Pistachios & Lemon Syrup

instructions.primary_message: Heat milk in a small saucepan set over medium heat until lukewarm. Transfer warm milk to a blender.

Add both flours, sugar, baking powder, yeast, and salt to the blender. Blend on high until the mixture is frothy, about 20 seconds. Place blender in a warm area (covered) and let batter rest, 30 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup all-purpose flour
½ cup semolina flour
2 tbsp granulated sugar
1 tsp baking powder
½ tsp instant dry yeast
½ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash, dry, and juice lemon into a medium saucepan. Add sugar, water, and rose or orange blossom water (optional), then stir to combine the syrup. Place over medium-high heat and cook, stirring occasionally, until the sugar completely dissolves. Remove from heat and set aside to cool to room temperature.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ lemon
granulated sugar
2 tsp rose water

instructions.primary_message: Place ricotta and 2 1/2 tablespoons of the cooled lemon syrup in a medium bowl. Stir to combine the cheese filling and set aside.
When the batter is done resting, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Once the skillet is hot, working in batches of 2 or 3 pancakes at a time, pour 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake into the skillet. Using the back of the spoon, spread the batter into 2-inch wide circles and cook until the bubbles on the top side are opaque and the bottom is golden brown (do not flip!). Transfer to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil to keep warm.

When all the pancakes are done, working one at a time, fold the pancakes in half and pinch the edges together with your fingers until halfway closed (forming a cone-like shape). Fill each pancake with a heaping tablespoon of the cheese filling, then transfer to a clean plate.
Mince pistachios and place in a small bowl. Dip the open end of the pancakes into the pistachios, gently pressing them into the cheese filling, then return to the plate.
Arrange the atayef on a serving platter and serve with lemon syrup for drizzling. Enjoy!
